newsitem.title: USA: G10, others agree to double IMF emergency funds.
newsitem.headline: G10, others agree to double IMF emergency funds.

text.p: The Group of 10 has reached basic agreement with rapidly developing nations on a plan to double the International Monetary Fund's emergency resources, a senior Canadian official said Saturday.
"Essentially agreement has been reached," the senior finance ministry official told reporters. "There are a few technical matters to be resolved."
The plan is aimed at boosting the money that the IMF can draw on in financial emergencies to about $50 billion through the creation of a New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB).
The final amount has not yet been worked out because the G10 is still talking with three or four potential participants in the plan, the Canadian official said. Among them are Chile and Hong Kong.
"We're hopeful that they will be able to join at the end of the day," he said.
Other countries that have agreed to join the NAB include Australia, Austria, Finland, Malaysia, Norway, Singapore, South Korea, Spain and Thailand.

The 11-nation G10 -- Belgium, Britain, Canada, France Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland and the United States -- already provide about $25 billion in emergency resources to the IMF.
